title: Data Protection Impact Assessment (DPIA)
description: A DPIA must be completed where an AI system is likely to result in a high risk to the rights and freedoms of natural persons (GDPR Art.35). This wizard captures the mandatory DPIA elements. The data types inventory produced here feeds directly into the Risk Assessment in Step 8.

sections.title: System description
sections.description: Describe the nature, scope, context, and purposes of the AI system's data processing.

fields.label: Processing description
fields.placeholder: Describe what the AI system does with personal data — what it receives, processes, and outputs.
fields.hint: Include: input data, model processing, output data, and any downstream use of AI output.

fields.label: Processing purposes
fields.placeholder: State the specific purposes for which personal data is processed by or through the AI system.
fields.hint: Be specific. Vague purposes (e.g. 'improve services') do not satisfy Art.35(7)(a).

fields.label: Vendor / AI provider data processing agreement in place?

sections.title: Data inventory
sections.description: Identify all personal data categories processed by the AI system. This inventory is used by the Risk Assessment in Step 8 to scope applicable risks.

fields.label: Data subjects
fields.hint: Select all categories of data subjects whose personal data the AI system processes.

fields.label: Personal data types processed
options: Financial data (salary, account numbers, transaction history)
Online identifiers (IP address, cookies, device IDs)

fields.label: Data retention period
fields.placeholder: e.g. 90 days / 7 years / duration of employment

sections.title: Special category data (Art.9)
sections.description: Special category data carries heightened obligations. Confirm whether any such data is involved and establish the Art.9(2) condition relied upon.

fields.label: Art.9(2) condition relied upon
options: Not applicable — no special category data
Art.9(2)(d) — Legitimate activities of a not-for-profit body
Art.9(2)(e) — Manifestly made public by the data subject
Art.9(2)(j) — Scientific / historical research or statistics

fields.label: Safeguards in place for special category data
fields.placeholder: Describe specific safeguards applied to special category data (e.g. encryption, access controls, anonymisation before AI processing).

sections.title: Lawful basis for processing
sections.description: Identify the Art.6 lawful basis for each processing purpose. A lawful basis must be established before processing begins.

fields.label: Primary lawful basis (Art.6)
options: Art.6(1)(c) — Compliance with a legal obligation

fields.label: Legitimate interests assessment (LIA) completed?
options: Not required — lawful basis is not Art.6(1)(f)

fields.label: Data subject notification mechanism
options: Privacy notice updated to include this processing
Specific notice provided at point of collection
Existing notice already covers this processing
Notice not yet updated — required before go-live
Not applicable (no direct collection from data subjects)

sections.title: Automated decision-making (Art.22)
sections.description: Art.22 applies where the AI system makes decisions based solely on automated processing that produce legal or similarly significant effects on individuals.

fields.label: Does the AI system make automated decisions with legal or similarly significant effects?
options: No — output is advisory only; human makes all decisions
Partially — AI output influences decisions but human reviews every case
Yes — AI output directly determines outcomes for individuals

fields.label: Art.22(2) ground relied upon
options: Not applicable — no Art.22 automated decisions
Art.22(2)(b) — Authorised by Union or Member State law

fields.label: Human oversight mechanism for automated decisions
fields.placeholder: Describe the human review checkpoint or override mechanism for decisions made by or significantly influenced by the AI system.
fields.hint: Art.22(3) requires the right to obtain human intervention, express one's point of view, and contest the decision where Art.22 applies.

fields.label: AI system explainability / transparency level
options: Full explainability — decision factors and weights are disclosed
Partial — high-level rationale provided to data subjects
Black-box — output only, no rationale available

sections.title: Data flows and third parties
sections.description: Map where personal data flows to and from, including any third-party AI providers or international transfers.

fields.label: Personal data transferred outside the EEA?
options: Yes — Standard Contractual Clauses (SCCs) in place
Yes — transfer mechanism not yet confirmed

fields.label: Third-party recipients / sub-processors
fields.placeholder: List all third parties (including AI vendor) that receive or process personal data as part of this AI system.

fields.label: Personal data used to train or fine-tune the AI model?
options: No — inference only; no training data retained by vendor
Yes — explicit consent or another basis obtained
Unknown — vendor contract does not address this

sections.title: Security measures
sections.description: Confirm the technical and organisational measures protecting personal data processed by the AI system.

fields.label: Technical security measures in place
options: Audit logging of access and processing
Data masking / pseudonymisation before AI input

fields.label: Data minimisation approach
fields.placeholder: Describe how personal data is minimised before being input to the AI system (e.g. anonymisation, pseudonymisation, field exclusion).

sections.title: Data subject rights
sections.description: Confirm that mechanisms exist to fulfil data subject rights, particularly given the complexity of AI-driven processing.

fields.label: Data subject rights fulfilment
options: Right to data portability (Art.20) — process documented
Rights re automated decisions (Art.22) — process documented

fields.label: Can personal data be erased from AI model outputs / logs?
options: Yes — erasure process confirmed with vendor
Partial — logs erased but model weights cannot be adjusted
fields.hint: AI systems may 'remember' training data in model weights. Confirm vendor's position on erasure requests.

sections.title: Necessity and proportionality
sections.description: Assess whether the processing is necessary for the stated purposes and proportionate to the risk it poses.

fields.label: Could the business purpose be achieved with less personal data or without AI?
options: No — AI and this level of data are necessary for the stated purpose
Partially — some data could be reduced; mitigation documented

fields.label: Proportionality and necessity statement
fields.placeholder: Justify why the scope of personal data processing by the AI system is proportionate to the business purpose.

sections.title: Risk identification and rating
sections.gdpr_ref: Art.35(7)(c) — risks to rights and freedoms
sections.description: Identify and rate the privacy risks posed by the AI system's processing. This rating feeds into the overall risk register in Step 8.

fields.label: Privacy risks identified
options: Unauthorised access to personal data via AI interface
Re-identification of pseudonymised data through AI inference
AI-generated output revealing personal data inadvertently
Bias / discriminatory outcomes affecting protected characteristics
Unlawful profiling or scoring of individuals
Personal data retained in AI model weights / caches
Data subject unaware of AI-driven processing
Inaccurate AI output used to make decisions about individuals
Vendor data breach or model exfiltration

fields.label: Residual risk justification
fields.placeholder: Justify the residual risk rating. Identify any risks that remain above acceptable threshold and the additional mitigations required.

sections.title: DPO consultation
sections.description: Where required, the DPO must be consulted on the DPIA. If residual risk is high and cannot be mitigated, the supervisory authority must be consulted under Art.36.

fields.label: DPO consulted?
options: No — DPO not required (no DPO designated)

fields.label: DPO advice / concerns
fields.placeholder: Record any DPO advice, conditions, or concerns raised during consultation.

fields.label: Supervisory authority consultation required (Art.36)?
fields.hint: Art.36 consultation is required where residual risk remains High or Very High after mitigation.

output_schema.description: Fields written to system-record['step-7'] on save

data_types_identified.description: Structured inventory used by Step 8 Risk Assessment
data_types_identified.standard_personal_data: array of selected personal data types
data_types_identified.special_category_data: array of selected special category types
data_types_identified.data_subjects: array of selected data subject categories

keys.answers: flat map of all field IDs to their values

requirement_labels: GDPR Art.35 — DPIA mandatory for high-risk processing
GDPR Art.36 — Prior consultation with supervisory authority
EU AI Act — High-risk AI system data governance
